photograph, the background job runs and writes the derived copy — then the
first reader to open the book triggers the same conversion again, and the
second copy is kept next to the first forever.

Make an upload get derived once. After the background work has run, opening
the book page and fetching the picture it links to does no image processing,
and exactly one derived copy is in storage.

What a reader is served does not change — the same picture they get today,
byte for byte.

**Analyzing the Codebase and Problem Statement**

Okay, first impression: this codebase is clean, which is a great starting point. Now, let's zero in on the problem description. This is really well-defined. It's a classic duplicate file issue, and the description makes it crystal clear: an editor uploads a picture, a background job processes it, but then a reader triggers the same conversion again, resulting in redundant storage. The goal is to ensure a single derived copy is created and served, without altering the reader's experience. Nice!

Alright, time to dive into the code. I need to get a comprehensive view, so I'll be meticulously reviewing these files: the models (`picture.rb`, `page.rb`, `leaf.rb`, `leafable.rb`, `book.rb`), the controllers (`pictures_controller.rb`, `action_text/markdown/uploads_controller.rb`), the helpers (`pictures_helper.rb`, `pages_helper.rb`, `leaves_helper.rb`, `books_helper.rb`), all of the views (within `pictures`, `leafables`, `leaves`, `books`, and `action_text/markdown/uploads`), the configuration files (`active_storage.rb`, `vips.rb`, `extensions.rb`, `markdown.rb`, `application.rb`, `routes.rb`, `storage.yml`), and supporting libraries (`markdown_renderer.rb`, `rails_ext/*`). This should give me a solid understanding of how images are uploaded, processed, stored, and served within the application. I need to understand the data flow completely.

class ActiveStorage::NamedVariant # :nodoc:
  attr_reader :transformations, :preprocessed

  def initialize(options)
    @preprocessed      = options[:preprocessed]
    @process_option    = options[:process]
    @transformations   = options.except(:preprocessed, :process)

    if options.key?(:preprocessed)
      ActiveStorage.deprecator.warn(<<~MSG.squish)
        The :preprocessed option is deprecated and will be removed in Rails 9.0.
        Use the :process option instead. Replace `preprocessed: true` with `process: :later`
        and `preprocessed: false` with `process: :lazily`.
      MSG
    end
  end

  def process(record)
    return @process_option if @process_option
    preprocessed?(record) ? :later : :lazily
  end

  private
    def preprocessed?(record)
      case preprocessed
      when Symbol
        record.send(preprocessed)
      when Proc
        preprocessed.call(record)
      else
        preprocessed
      end
    end
end

require "marcel"

# = Active Storage \Variation
#
# A set of transformations that can be applied to a blob to create a variant. This class is exposed via
# the ActiveStorage::Blob#variant method and should rarely be used directly.
#
# In case you do need to use this directly, it's instantiated using a hash of transformations where
# the key is the command and the value is the arguments. Example:
#
#   ActiveStorage::Variation.new(resize_to_limit: [100, 100], colourspace: "b-w", rotate: "-90", saver: { trim: true })
#
# The options map directly to {ImageProcessing}[https://github.com/janko/image_processing] commands.
class ActiveStorage::Variation
  attr_reader :transformations

  class << self
    # Returns a Variation instance based on the given variator. If the variator is a Variation, it is
    # returned unmodified. If it is a String, it is passed to ActiveStorage::Variation.decode. Otherwise,
    # it is assumed to be a transformations Hash and is passed directly to the constructor.
    def wrap(variator)
      case variator
      when self
        variator
      when String
        decode variator
      else
        new variator
      end
    end

    # Returns a Variation instance with the transformations that were encoded by +encode+.
    def decode(key)
      new ActiveStorage.verifier.verify(key, purpose: :variation)
    end

    # Returns a signed key for the +transformations+, which can be used to refer to a specific
    # variation in a URL or combined key (like <tt>ActiveStorage::Variant#key</tt>).
    def encode(transformations)
      ActiveStorage.verifier.generate(transformations, purpose: :variation)
    end
  end

  def initialize(transformations)
    @transformations = transformations.deep_symbolize_keys
  end

  def default_to(defaults)
    self.class.new transformations.reverse_merge(defaults)
  end

  # Accepts a File object, performs the +transformations+ against it, and
  # saves the transformed image into a temporary file.
  def transform(file, &block)
    ActiveSupport::Notifications.instrument("transform.active_storage") do
      transformer.transform(file, format: format, &block)
    end
  end

  def format
    transformations.fetch(:format, :png).tap do |format|
      if Marcel::Magic.by_extension(format.to_s).nil?
        raise ArgumentError, "Invalid variant format (#{format.inspect})"
      end
    end
  end

  def content_type
    Marcel::MimeType.for(extension: format.to_s)
  end

  # Returns a signed key for all the +transformations+ that this variation was instantiated with.
  def key
    self.class.encode(transformations)
  end

  def digest
    OpenSSL::Digest::SHA1.base64digest Marshal.dump(transformations)
  end

  private
    def transformer
      ActiveStorage.variant_transformer.new(transformations.except(:format))
    end
end

class ActiveStorage::CreateVariantsJob < ActiveStorage::BaseJob
  queue_as { ActiveStorage.queues[:transform] }

  discard_on ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
  retry_on ActiveStorage::IntegrityError, attempts: 10, wait: :polynomially_longer

  def perform(blob, variants:, process:)
    @blob = blob
    @process = process

    create_preview_image if preview_image_needed?

    variants.each do |transformations|
      ActiveStorage::TransformJob.public_send(perform_method, @blob, transformations)
    end
  end

  private
    def create_preview_image
      @blob.preview({}).processed
    end

    def preview_image_needed?
      @blob.previewable? && !@blob.preview_image.attached?
    end

    def perform_method
      (@process == :immediately) ? :perform_now : :perform_later
    end
end

  queue_as { ActiveStorage.queues[:transform] }

# = Active Storage \Variant With Record
#
# Like an ActiveStorage::Variant, but keeps detail about the variant in the database as an
# ActiveStorage::VariantRecord. This is used if +ActiveStorage.track_variants+ is enabled.
class ActiveStorage::VariantWithRecord
  include ActiveStorage::Blob::Servable

  attr_reader :blob, :variation
  delegate :service, to: :blob
  delegate :content_type, to: :variation

  def initialize(blob, variation)
    @blob, @variation = blob, ActiveStorage::Variation.wrap(variation)
  end

  def processed
    process unless processed?
    self
  end

  def image
    record&.image
  end

  def filename
    ActiveStorage::Filename.new "#{blob.filename.base}.#{variation.format.downcase}"
  end

  # Destroys record and deletes file from service.
  def destroy
    record&.destroy
  end

  delegate :key, :url, :download, to: :image, allow_nil: true

  # Returns true if the variant has already been processed and stored.
  def processed?
    record.present?
  end

  # Process the variant from a local io, avoiding a download from the service.
  # This is an optimization for when the original file is still available locally
  # (e.g., during the initial upload flow).
  def process_from_io(io) # :nodoc:
    return if processed?

    variation.transform(io) do |output|
      create_or_find_record(image: {
        io: output,
        filename: "#{blob.filename.base}.#{variation.format.downcase}",
        content_type: variation.content_type,
        service_name: blob.service.name
      })
    end
  end

  private
    def process
      transform_blob { |image| create_or_find_record(image: image) }
    end

    def transform_blob
      blob.open do |input|
        variation.transform(input) do |output|
          yield io: output, filename: "#{blob.filename.base}.#{variation.format.downcase}",
            content_type: variation.content_type, service_name: blob.service.name
        end
      end
    end

    def create_or_find_record(image:)
      @record =
        ActiveRecord::Base.connected_to(role: ActiveRecord.writing_role) do
          blob.variant_records.create_or_find_by!(variation_digest: variation.digest) do |record|
            record.image.attach(image)
          end
        end
    end

    def record
      @record ||= if blob.variant_records.loaded?
        blob.variant_records.find { |v| v.variation_digest == variation.digest }
      else
        blob.variant_records.find_by(variation_digest: variation.digest)
      end
    end
end

My initial reaction was *whoa*, ActiveJob keeps the `:webp` symbol, which *should* mean the format is preserved all the way through. But, let's trace this step by step. I'm seeing a potential issue when ActiveStorage's verifier comes into play. 1. **Variant Creation:** The `NamedVariant` is correctly storing transformations including `format: :webp` (as a Symbol). The upload job and subsequent background processing also seem to handle this correctly thanks to ActiveJob's serialization. 2. **The Background Process:** The `ActiveStorage::CreateVariantsJob` fires up the `ActiveStorage::TransformJob`, which uses that transformation hash, which STILL contains `:webp` (a symbol). The `VariantWithRecord#process` ends up computing a digest based on the symbolized transformations including the correct `:webp` symbol, and writes a `.webp` file to storage and a `ActiveStorage::VariantRecord` with the expected digest. This looks good, so far. 3. **The Reader's Request:** Now, when a reader opens the page and the `image_tag` helper is used, it generates a URL that includes the `variation_key`. That `variation_key` gets encoded using `ActiveStorage.verifier`. *This* is where the trouble begins. In Rails 7.1+, the default serializer is JSON. JSON *stringifies* the `:webp` symbol into the string "webp". 4. **The Decode:** When the reader's browser requests the image URL, the controller uses the encoded `variation_key`. `ActiveStorage.verifier.verify` parses the JSON, and boom - the `:format` is now a string "webp" (not a symbol) after `deep_symbolize_keys`. Therefore, the `variation.digest` computed with the STRING "webp" doesn't match the digest of the original variant computed with the SYMBOL `:webp`. The `processed?` check fails. The system re-processes the image *again*, creating a *duplicate* .webp file with a *different* digest and persisting the duplicate record in the database. **Wait, let me make sure I understand the prompt** The key problem is the reader is triggering the transformation *again*, even when it should be pulling a pre-processed variant, and that's resulting in duplicate storage. **Deep Dive into Active Storage and WebP Variant Processing**

Okay, here's what I've got after this meticulous examination. It looks like we have three models utilizing Active Storage attachments: `Book`, `ActionText::Markdown::Uploads`, and `Picture`.  `Picture` is the only one generating image variants, specifically a "large" variant using `resize_to_limit: [1500, 1500]` and `format: :webp`.  Let's trace how this plays out in the application.

When a photograph is uploaded and the 'Picture' model is saved, the initial upload stores the original image.  A background job (`ActiveStorage::CreateVariantsJob`) is then enqueued with the specified transformations. Inside the job, `ActiveJob::Serializers::SymbolSerializer` will convert the symbol `:webp` into a string. The job `ActiveStorage::TransformJob` is then started with the specified transformations to generate the variant. Crucially, the transformation process utilizes Vips to create the `.webp` version using `format: :webp`.  The `variation.digest` is computed using Marshal for our current `:webp` symbol.

Now, when a reader accesses the image, the `image_tag` helper generates a URL for the variant.  This URL points to `/rails/active_storage/representations/redirect`, which triggers the `ActiveStorage::Representations::RedirectController`. This controller retrieves the *processed* representation. The crucial point here is how the `variation_key` is generated and *decoded*.   Active Storage uses a `MessageVerifier` to encode and decode the transformations.  The current configuration is `:json_allow_marshal`, which serializes the transformations, *regardless* of whether the original `format` was a symbol (`:webp`) or a string (`"webp"`), *as JSON*. The JSON would produce the same `variation_key`.

Therefore, the critical point is that, regardless of whether the developer used `:webp` or `"webp"`, the end result *should* be the same. The JSON representation ensures that the same variant is requested and created or retrieved.

However, I need to confirm this. I must now rigorously test in `bin/rails runner` to verify that `ActiveStorage::Variation.encode({ resize_to_limit: [ 1500, 1500 ], format: :webp })` and `ActiveStorage::Variation.encode({ resize_to_limit: [ 1500, 1500 ], format: "webp" })` generate the identical `variation_key`.  Furthermore, I must confirm that `ImageProcessing::Vips.convert("webp")` and `ImageProcessing::Vips.convert(:webp)` generate the same file content, byte-for-byte.  If this is true, then we are safe and there's no problem.

**Deep Dive into Potential ActiveStorage Variant Duplication**

Okay, hold on a second! Let me re-trace my steps and critically assess how we're handling image variants within ActiveStorage. I need to make sure I'm not missing anything. I've got a hunch there's a problem with duplicate processing of images, and I need to methodically track down the root cause.

First, let's revisit `ActiveStorage::Blob::Representable`. I need to re-examine what `default_variant_format` returns. Right, I remember now! In `blob/representable.rb`, `format` can be a STRING, like `"webp"`, `"jpg"`, or `"png"`, especially for web images!

Then, I see it in `variant_with_record.rb`, the `filename` method that uses `variation.format.downcase`. The crucial bit here is that `.downcase` handles *both* Symbols (which it converts to strings) *and* strings, which is smart design.

And in `variation.rb`, the `format` method calls `transformations.fetch(:format, :png)`. This then tries to validate the format by extension with `Marcel::Magic.by_extension`. That's where we make sure we have a valid format. However, if that fetch is `:png` and the underlying format is `"webp"` *could* be a spot that might create the issue.

Now, let's play devil's advocate and dig a bit deeper. I need to think like a truly skeptical engineer and look for other places where a duplicate operation could be triggered.

### Question 1: How does a leaf get edited, specifically in `Leaf::Editable`?

Alright, let's rewind and see how things get updated in the `Leaf::Editable` module, specifically in `app/models/leaf/editable.rb`. The flow, as I recall, is:
1.  We have `update_without_recording_edit` which is used if we can get away without making a new copy of the leafable and all of its attached resources.
2.  We also have `update_and_record_edit` which is used if the leafable needs to be updated. This creates a new leafable copy.

Now, let's think about an editor uploading an image. Let's trace it in Writebook:
1.  An editor clicks to add a new image page, `LeafablesController#create` creates a new instance.
2.  Then, later, the editor opens the image for editing and uploads a file. The `leafable_params` will include the uploaded file.

Inside `Leaf::Editable#edit`:
*   `will_change_leafable?(leafable_params)` returns `true` because the image parameter is changing.
*   `edits.empty?` is `true`.

So `update_and_record_edit` is called. It creates a copy of the leafable *and* attaches any existing attachments. If the editor uploads *after* an image was already present, `new.image.attach(old_blob)` attaches the old blob. That `old_blob` *already* has a `variant_record`, so `CreateVariantsJob` *should* call `VariantWithRecord#processed` and *should* notice it's already done and skip!

But what *if* the `old_blob` is *not* detected as `processed? == true`?

### Question 2: Is the error with `Picture`'s `format`, or something else?

Now, let's take a HUGE step back, and ask the BIG questions:
Is the problem really in `app/models/picture.rb` (`format: :webp` vs `"webp"`), OR is it potentially in `ActiveStorage::Variation`, `config/initializers/active_storage.rb`, or other conventions? Let's check EVERYTHING in the code to check for the proper style of the codebase and any hints. Let's see if something is causing an unexpected format.

require "vips"
require "tempfile"

# libvips selects a loader from a file's actual bytes, not from its declared content type. These
# tests pin which loader is selected for each file type under the app's configured loader policy
# (config/initializers/vips.rb).
class VipsLoaderPolicyTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  # Header bytes are enough for libvips to identify a format; native types are encoded live, exotic
  # ones are represented by their magic bytes.
  FTYP_AVIF = "\x00\x00\x00\x1cftypavif\x00\x00\x00\x00avifmif1miaf".b
  FTYP_HEIC = "\x00\x00\x00\x1cftypheic\x00\x00\x00\x00heicmif1miaf".b
  BMP = "BM" + [ 0, 0, 54 ].pack("V3") + "\x00" * 40
  PSD = "8BPS" + [ 1 ].pack("n") + "\x00" * 26
  ICO = "\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00" + "\x00" * 16
  SVG = %q(<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="8" height="8"/>)

  test "loads PNG" do
    assert_equal "VipsForeignLoadPngFile", loader_for(encode("png"))
  end

  test "loads GIF" do
    assert_equal "VipsForeignLoadNsgifFile", loader_for(encode("gif"))
  end

  test "loads JPEG" do
    assert_equal "VipsForeignLoadJpegFile", loader_for(encode("jpg"))
  end

  test "loads TIFF" do
    assert_equal "VipsForeignLoadTiffFile", loader_for(encode("tif"))
  end

  test "loads WebP" do
    assert_equal "VipsForeignLoadWebpFile", loader_for(encode("webp"))
  end

  test "loads AVIF" do
    assert_equal "VipsForeignLoadHeifFile", loader_for(FTYP_AVIF)
  end

  test "loads HEIC" do
    assert_equal "VipsForeignLoadHeifFile", loader_for(FTYP_HEIC)
  end

  test "denies BMP through magickload" do
    assert_nil loader_for(BMP)
  end

  test "denies PSD through magickload" do
    assert_nil loader_for(PSD)
  end

  test "denies ICO through magickload" do
    assert_nil loader_for(ICO)
  end

  test "denies SVG through svgload" do
    assert_nil loader_for(SVG)
  end

  test "denies OpenSlide files through openslideload" do
    # OpenSlide files can segfault the embedded sqlite in forked parallel workers
    assert_loader_blocked :openslideload, ".svs"
  end

  test "denies FITS files through fitsload" do
    assert_loader_blocked :fitsload, ".fits"
  end

  test "denies MATLAB files through matload" do
    assert_loader_blocked :matload, ".mat"
  end

  test "denies NIFTI files through niftiload" do
    assert_loader_blocked :niftiload, ".nii"
  end

  test "denies RAW files through dcrawload" do
    assert_loader_blocked :dcrawload, ".raw"
  end

  test "denies VIPS files through vipsload" do
    assert_loader_blocked :vipsload, ".vips"
  end

  private
    # Invoke a specific libvips loader directly and assert it is refused because the
    # operation is blocked (rather than because the bytes are not a valid image).
    def assert_loader_blocked(operation, extension)
      Tempfile.create([ "blocked_loader", extension ], binmode: true) do |file|
        file.write "not an image"
        file.flush

        error = assert_raises(Vips::Error) { Vips::Image.public_send(operation, file.path) }
        actual = error.message.chomp

        # note that exception message may include multiple errors on separate lines,
        # so `^` and `$` anchors are used instead of `\A` and `\z`.
        if actual =~ /^VipsOperation: class \"#{operation}\" not found$/
          skip "libvips does not support #{operation} on this system"
        end
        assert_match(/^#{operation}: operation is blocked$/, actual)
      end
    end

    def encode(ext)
      Vips::Image.black(8, 8).add(128).cast("uchar").write_to_buffer(".#{ext}")
    end

    def loader_for(bytes)
      Tempfile.create(%w[loader_probe .img], binmode: true) do |file|
        file.write bytes
        file.flush
        Vips.vips_foreign_find_load(file.path)
      end
    end
end

  test "denies VIPS files through vipsload" do
    assert_loader_blocked :vipsload, ".vips"
  end

  private
    # Invoke a specific libvips loader directly and assert it is refused because the
    # operation is blocked (rather than because the bytes are not a valid image).
    def assert_loader_blocked(operation, extension)
      Tempfile.create([ "blocked_loader", extension ], binmode: true) do |file|
        file.write "not an image"
        file.flush

        error = assert_raises(Vips::Error) { Vips::Image.public_send(operation, file.path) }
        actual = error.message.chomp

        # note that exception message may include multiple errors on separate lines,
        # so `^` and `$` anchors are used instead of `\A` and `\z`.
        if actual =~ /^VipsOperation: class \"#{operation}\" not found$/
          skip "libvips does not support #{operation} on this system"
        end
        assert_match(/^#{operation}: operation is blocked$/, actual)
      end
    end

    def encode(ext)
      Vips::Image.black(8, 8).add(128).cast("uchar").write_to_buffer(".#{ext}")
    end

    def loader_for(bytes)
      Tempfile.create(%w[loader_probe .img], binmode: true) do |file|
        file.write bytes
        file.flush
        Vips.vips_foreign_find_load(file.path)
      end
    end

require_relative "/app/test/test_helper" rescue require "./test/test_helper"

class ReproduceDuplicatePictureTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  test "reproduce duplicate picture derivation" do
    transforms = []
    subscriber = ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe("transform.active_storage") do |*args|
      transforms << ActiveSupport::Notifications::Event.new(*args)
    end

    sign_in :kevin

    leaf = leaves(:reading_picture)
    photo_path = Rails.root.join("app/assets/images/demo/writebook-manual.jpg")
    uploaded_photo = Rack::Test::UploadedFile.new(photo_path, "image/jpeg")

    perform_enqueued_jobs do
      put leafable_path(leaf), params: {
        leaf: { title: "Uploaded Photo" },
        picture: { image: uploaded_photo }
      }
      assert_response :no_content
    end

    picture = leaf.reload.picture
    original_blob = picture.image.blob

    puts "=== AFTER UPLOAD + BACKGROUND JOBS ==="
    puts "Transforms performed so far: #{transforms.size}"
    puts "VariantRecord count for blob: #{original_blob.variant_records.count}"
    puts "VariantRecord digests: #{original_blob.variant_records.pluck(:variation_digest).inspect}"
    variant_blobs_after_job = original_blob.variant_records.map { |vr| vr.image.blob }
    puts "Derived files in storage: #{variant_blobs_after_job.map { |b| [b.key, service_file_exists?(b.key), b.byte_size] }.inspect}"

    transforms_before_reader = transforms.size

    # Reader opens the book page and fetches the picture it links to
    sign_out
    sign_in :jz

    get book_slug_path(books(:handbook))
    assert_response :ok

    img_src = css_select("##{dom_id(leaf)} .toc__thumbnail img").first["src"]
    puts "Book page img src: #{img_src}"

    # Also check leafable page img src
    get leafable_slug_path(leaf)
    assert_response :ok
    leaf_img_src = css_select("figure.page--picture img").first["src"]
    puts "Picture page img src: #{leaf_img_src}"

    # Fetch the picture linked from the book page
    get img_src
    assert_response :redirect
    redirect_target = response.redirect_url
    puts "Representation redirect target: #{redirect_target}"

    get redirect_target
    assert_response :ok
    served_bytes = response.body
    puts "Served bytesize: #{served_bytes.bytesize}, SHA256: #{ Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(served_bytes) }"

    puts "=== AFTER READER FETCHES PICTURE ==="
    puts "Transforms triggered by reader: #{transforms.size - transforms_before_reader}"
    original_blob.reload
    puts "VariantRecord count for blob: #{original_blob.variant_records.count}"
    puts "VariantRecord digests: #{original_blob.variant_records.pluck(:variation_digest).inspect}"
    variant_blobs_after_reader = original_blob.variant_records.map { |vr| vr.image.blob }
    puts "Derived files in storage: #{variant_blobs_after_reader.map { |b| [b.key, service_file_exists?(b.key), b.byte_size] }.inspect}"

    assert_equal 1, transforms.size, "Expected upload to be derived only once"
    assert_equal 0, transforms.size - transforms_before_reader, "Expected reader request to do no image processing"
    assert_equal 1, original_blob.variant_records.count, "Expected exactly one derived copy in storage"
  ensure
    ActiveSupport::Notifications.unsubscribe(subscriber) if subscriber
  end

  private
    def service_file_exists?(key)
      ActiveStorage::Blob.service.exist?(key)
    end
end
EOF

require "./test/test_helper"
require "vips"

class EdgeCasesPictureDerivationTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  test "large >1500px JPEG, PNG, WebP, and TIFF each get derived once and match byte-for-byte" do
    [
      [ "photo.jpg", "image/jpeg", Vips::Image.black(2000, 1600).add([ 120, 80, 200 ]).cast("uchar").write_to_buffer(".jpg") ],
      [ "diagram.png", "image/png", Vips::Image.black(1800, 1200).add([ 10, 150, 90 ]).cast("uchar").write_to_buffer(".png") ],
      [ "existing.webp", "image/webp", File.binread(Rails.root.join("test/fixtures/files/white-rabbit.webp")) ],
      [ "scan.tif", "image/tiff", Vips::Image.black(600, 400).add(128).cast("uchar").write_to_buffer(".tif") ]
    ].each do |filename, content_type, raw_bytes|
      # Compute reference bytes using original :webp Variation decoded via URL (what reader got before)
      old_key = ActiveStorage::Variation.encode(format: :webp, resize_to_limit: [ 1500, 1500 ])
      expected_bytes = Tempfile.create([ "src", File.extname(filename) ], binmode: true) do |tf|
        tf.write(raw_bytes)
        tf.rewind
        ActiveStorage::Variation.decode(old_key).transform(tf) { |out| out.read }
      end

      transforms = 0
      sub = ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe("transform.active_storage") { transforms += 1 }

      begin
        sign_in :kevin
        books(:handbook).update!(published: true)

        Tempfile.create([ "upload", File.extname(filename) ], binmode: true) do |tf|
          tf.write(raw_bytes)
          tf.flush

          blobs_before = ActiveStorage::Blob.count
          variants_before = ActiveStorage::VariantRecord.count

          perform_enqueued_jobs do
            post book_pictures_path(books(:handbook), format: :turbo_stream), params: {
              leaf: { title: "Title #{filename}" },
              picture: { image: Rack::Test::UploadedFile.new(tf.path, content_type), caption: "Cap" }
            }
            assert_response :success
          end

          # 1 original blob + 1 derived variant blob = 2 blobs total
          assert_equal 1, transforms, "Expected 1 transform during background job for #{filename}"
          assert_equal blobs_before + 2, ActiveStorage::Blob.count, "Expected 1 original + 1 derived blob for #{filename}"
          assert_equal variants_before + 1, ActiveStorage::VariantRecord.count, "Expected 1 VariantRecord for #{filename}"

          leaf = books(:handbook).leaves.last
          sign_out

          # Unauthenticated reader opens book page
          get book_slug_path(books(:handbook))
          assert_response :ok
          toc_img_src = css_select("##{dom_id(leaf)} .toc__thumbnail img").first["src"]

          # Unauthenticated reader opens picture leafable page
          get leafable_slug_path(leaf)
          assert_response :ok
          page_img_src = css_select("figure.page--picture img").first["src"]
          page_link_href = css_select("figure.page--picture a").first["href"]

          assert_equal URI(toc_img_src).path, URI(page_img_src).path

          # Reader fetches derived picture
          get page_img_src
          assert_response :redirect
          get response.redirect_url
          assert_response :ok
          assert_equal expected_bytes, response.body, "Served bytes changed for #{filename}!"

          # Reader also fetches full-res link
          get page_link_href
          assert_response :redirect
          get response.redirect_url
          assert_response :ok
          assert_equal raw_bytes, response.body

          # Still 1 transform, 1 derived copy!
          assert_equal 1, transforms, "Expected 0 additional transforms on reader requests for #{filename}"
          assert_equal blobs_before + 2, ActiveStorage::Blob.count, "Expected no extra blobs for #{filename}"
          assert_equal variants_before + 1, ActiveStorage::VariantRecord.count, "Expected still 1 VariantRecord for #{filename}"
        end
      ensure
        ActiveSupport::Notifications.unsubscribe(sub)
      end
    end
  end
end
EOF

## Testing Conventions

### Use Existing Fixtures
Prefer using existing fixtures over creating new records in tests. For example, use `leaves(:welcome_page)` instead of `books(:handbook).press Page.new(body: "..."), title: "..."`.

### URL Helpers in Tests
Use `_path` helpers instead of `_url` helpers in controller/integration tests unless you need to test across different hosts or explicitly need the full URL.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
get book_slug_path(books(:handbook))
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
get book_slug_url(books(:handbook))
```

### Response Body Assertions
Use `assert_in_body` and `assert_not_in_body` to check if text is present or absent in the response body without DOM manipulation.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
assert_in_body "Expected content"
assert_not_in_body "Unexpected content"
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
assert_includes response.body, "Expected content"
assert_not_includes response.body, "Unexpected content"
```

## Controller Conventions

### Simplified respond_to Blocks
When using `respond_to` with default rendering, omit the `{ render }` block as it's implied.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
def show
  respond_to do |format|
    format.html
    format.md
  end
end
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
def show
  respond_to do |format|
    format.html { render }
    format.md { render }
  end
end
```

require "test_helper"

class PictureTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "markable returns caption" do
    picture = Picture.new(caption: "A great picture")

    assert_equal "A great picture", picture.markable
  end

  test "markable returns nil when caption is nil" do
    picture = Picture.new(caption: nil)

    assert_nil picture.markable
  end

  test "large_image is the resized variant of a variable image" do
    assert_kind_of ActiveStorage::VariantWithRecord, pictures(:reading).large_image
  end

  test "large_image variation digest matches representation decoded from variation key" do
    variant = pictures(:reading).large_image
    decoded = pictures(:reading).image.blob.representation(variant.variation.key)

    assert_equal variant.variation.digest, decoded.variation.digest
  end

  test "large_image is the original image when the image cannot be resized" do
    picture = pictures(:reading)
    picture.image.attach io: file_fixture("pixel.bmp").open, filename: "pixel.bmp", content_type: "image/bmp"

    assert_equal picture.image, picture.large_image
  end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > test/controllers/pictures_controller_test.rb
require "test_helper"

class PicturesControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    sign_in :kevin
  end

  test "update picture" do
    get edit_leafable_path(leaves(:reading_picture))
    assert_response :ok

    put leafable_path(leaves(:reading_picture)), params: {
      leaf: { title: "New picture" },
      picture: {
        image: fixture_file_upload("white-rabbit.webp", "image/webp")
      } }

    assert_response :no_content

    updated_picture = Picture.last
    assert_equal "New picture", updated_picture.title
    assert_equal "white-rabbit.webp", updated_picture.image.filename.to_s
  end

  test "uploaded picture is derived once in the background and reused when fetched by a reader" do
    leaf = leaves(:reading_picture)

    assert_notifications_count("transform.active_storage", 1) do
      perform_enqueued_jobs do
        put leafable_path(leaf), params: {
          leaf: { title: "Uploaded photograph" },
          picture: {
            image: fixture_file_upload("white-rabbit.webp", "image/webp")
          } }
        assert_response :no_content
      end
    end

    blob = leaf.reload.picture.image.blob
    assert_equal 1, blob.variant_records.count
    derived_bytes = blob.variant_records.sole.image.download

    sign_out
    sign_in :jz

    assert_no_notifications("transform.active_storage") do
      assert_no_changes -> { ActiveStorage::Blob.count } do
        get book_slug_path(books(:handbook))
        assert_response :ok
        toc_image_src = css_select("##{dom_id(leaf)} .toc__thumbnail img").first["src"]

        get leafable_slug_path(leaf)
        assert_response :ok
        page_image_src = css_select("figure.page--picture img").first["src"]

        assert_equal toc_image_src, page_image_src

        get page_image_src
        assert_response :redirect
        follow_redirect!
        assert_response :ok
        assert_equal derived_bytes, response.body
      end
    end

    assert_equal 1, blob.reload.variant_records.count
  end

  test "update caption" do
    get edit_leafable_path(leaves(:reading_picture))
    assert_response :ok

    put leafable_path(leaves(:reading_picture)), params: {
      picture: {
        caption: "New caption"
      } }

    assert_response :no_content

    updated_picture = Picture.last

    assert_equal "New caption", updated_picture.caption
    assert_equal "reading.webp", updated_picture.image.filename.to_s
  end
end
EOF

messages.content: I have resolved the duplicate picture variant issue: ### Root Cause `Picture` declared its `:large` variant with a symbol format (`format: :webp`): - During background preprocessing (`process: :later`), `ActiveJob` preserves symbol values via `SymbolSerializer`, so `ActiveStorage::TransformJob` computed `variation.digest` (`Marshal.dump(transformations)`) with `format: :webp`. - When rendering `` URLs, `ActiveStorage.verifier` encodes the transformations as JSON, serializing `:webp` to `"webp"`. When `ActiveStorage::Representations::RedirectController` decoded `params[:variation_key]`, `ActiveStorage::Variation` symbolized only hash keys (`deep_symbolize_keys`), leaving `format: "webp"` as a `String`. - Because `Marshal.dump` produces different bytes for `:webp` vs `"webp"`, the representation request missed the `ActiveStorage::VariantRecord` created by the background job, re-ran the Vips conversion synchronously, and stored a second derived `.webp` file alongside the first forever. ### Fix - Changed `format: :webp` to `format: "webp"` in `app/models/picture.rb` so that the background job, in-memory `Picture#large_image`, and URL-decoded representation all produce the exact same `variation.digest`, URL `variation_key`, and byte-for-byte derived WebP output. - Added model and integration tests in `test/models/picture_test.rb` and `test/controllers/pictures_controller_test.rb` verifying that an upload is derived once in the background and reused with zero additional image processing or storage copies when opened and fetched by a reader.
